author: GraphicFade
prev: This mod introduces Fade , a neutral traveling merchant designed to provide a mobile trade solution during your journey. Fade appears periodically to offer basic supplies and provide a way for you to offload excess gear without needing to backtrack to a major hub.
text: Spawning Mechanics Fade operates on a cycle, appearing roughly every 38 to 76 minutes . Once he spawns, he stays in the world for 5 minutes before de-spawning. To ensure he doesn't interfere with the flow of the game, Fade will never appear while you are in combat, engaged in dialogue, or resting at camp.
next: As a neutral NPC, Fade is ignored by hostile entities, so he won’t be targeted during combat. Note that he is also not pickpocketable, keeping your interactions strictly professional. His Attitude Resets each encounter.

author: indefiance
prev: New Work vs Duplication The Cathedral view vastly reduces duplication of effort – instead promoting either improvements in, or extensions of the original, or the creation of entirely new, complementary works. One doesn't have go far in reviewing one's mod library to see quite a few of these examples
text: Perfection vs Stagnation The Cathedral view tends towards perfection, while the Parlor view tends towards repetition and stagnation. Repetition, because earlier useful works that have been closed off have to be recreated. Stagnation, because this fails to lead to improvements, and more importantly because few modders are interested in replicating something that has already been done before. (Especially since, if they knew of the original, they probably have a copy of the original mod, and hence have no personal need to recreate it.

author: Sandiford
heading: Swashbuckler
prev: Metamagic access changed. Previously: L2: 2 L3: 3 L10: 4
text: Now: L2: 1 L3: 2 L5: 3 L9: 4 Delaying access to metamagic has some benefits - firstly the metamagic list for level 3+ has more options than at level 2, so this grants more picks from the extended list. Secondly it gives you more time to get familiar with the character before picking metamagics, making it easier to pick metamagics that synergise with your spells, rather than having to choose half your metamagics before you've even got level 2 spells. Lastly, this gives sorcs more progression over the course of the game.
next: Metamagic level 2 and level 3+ lists have been changed to be more appropriate to the level where they are available. Subtle spell available at L2, Twinned spell moved back to L3. The high list is now the low list plus Twinned, Heightened, and Quickened.

author: Doresain
heading: Compatibility & Risks
prev: 1. Base game overrides : To get sorting to work correctly, I had to override ~25 items from the base game. To get the companions' bags into their starting inventory, I had to override their starting inventories. What are the risks from this?
text: If another mod you're using modifies the same files, whichever one is last in the load order will override the changes made by the other. In the case of this mod, if my changes are overwritten by another mod some items will not sort correctly anymore and companions may spawn without bags.
next: If Larian changes these items in a patch, my old version of the item will override their new one. This could have no impact or it could completely break the game or anything in between.

author: osirisofinternet
prev: When Does AIM Manage Items? Unless an item is in AIM's blacklist, or inside a blacklisted container, Items will be processed when being added directly to a party member's inventory - this includes picking up, transferring between party members, pulling out of containers. Items already in a given cha
text: It will also attempt to sort all items on load (if they haven't been sorted previously) - this functionality is a little unreliable due to the sheer amount of items being processed and Larian's Event pipeline, so you'll probably have to manually sort items yourself first, or drop and pick them up, to get your inventory where you want it to be (only needs to happen the very first time you load up with AIM). Make sure to save!
next: To prevent constant reprocessing, a custom tag is added to each item that is evaluated by AIM, regardless of whether it was eligible for sorting. This tag can be cleared by dropping the item, allowing it to be re-processed on pickup.

author: magnetuning
prev: Install the .PAK file versions via BG3 Mod Manager. You can leave them in the Overrides section; mod load order shouldn't matter. Install the loose file versions by dragging the Public folder in the .zip files into your BG3 Data folder.
text: Uninstall the .PAKs by removing them completely from your BG3 Mods folder. They're overrides, so they'll still affect your game if they're in that folder, even if they're not in your active mod load order. Uninstall the loose files by removing them from your BG3 Data folder. Only install either the .PAK or the loose file format of a given version of the mod! (i.e. if you have the .PAK version of Stop Yelling Please - Elfsong, don't install the loose files at the same time.) Nothing bad will happen if you do, it's just unnecessary to have both.
next: It's fine to mix and match between .PAKs and loose file formats of the different versions of the mod, though, if you'd like. If you want to have the .PAK format of the Circus of the Last Days version, but loose files for the Main version, that's totally fine.

author: NellsRelo
prev: Compatibility Subclass mods are notoriously incompatible, however, this mod uses the Compatibility Framework API to ensure compatibility with other Monk subclass mods as long as the Framework is installed. It also has a fallback, in case the CF is not installed, which replicates CF functionality.
text: If you're a mod author and want to know how this is done, feel free to take a look at the Github, in the Script Extender Bootstrapping files. Note that using the CF is ideal, as the CF caches each Progression that it works with, preventing unnecessary calls to the game files, preventing major performance issues. The fallback should only be used if the CF is not detected in the user's load order.
next: Installation This mod relies on the Community Library and the BG3 Script Extender. See the Requirements section for details.

mod: EasyCam BG3 Camera Toggle AHK Script
author: Az0iC0
heading: How It Works:
prev: To address this, the script incorporates a strategic sequence: upon activating the toggle with the side button (XButton1), it simulates a right mouse button click. This simulated click is necessary for the game to properly recognize and respond to the toggle effect on the side button.
text: However, clicking the right mouse button in BG3 typically commands the character to move to the clicked location. To counteract this unintended movement, the script swiftly presses and releases the 'W' key. This quick action cancels the character's movement command while maintaining the desired camera follow effect. (This only works in conjunction with the WASD mod, recommended install WASD mod.)
next: The script ensures there are small delays between each action (side button press, right-click, and 'W' press) to match the game's response timings and ensure seamless execution.

prev: Version 1.1 After playing around for a bit, I've found that the downside to Invisibility is that enemies usually don't even bother trying to attack you. This makes combat too trivial. So instead, I've added two additional spells to use instead:
text: Unlimited Blur: allows you to cast Blur without consuming an action or a spellslot, without using concentration. This allows you to impose Disadvantage on incoming attacks against you without preventing them like Invisibility. The downside is that without concentration, the buff can't be easily removed if you move out of the darkness area.
next: Unlimited TrueStrike: allows you to cast TrueStrike without consuming an action, without using concentration. This allows you to gain Advantage on your attack.

heading: Compatibility
prev: This mod patches the target conditions of hundreds of spells, including ones added by mods. This is required to implement Twinned Spell's new criteria without my having to be aware of every spell mod in existence.
text: Patching is done dynamically on startup via Script Extender and shouldn't cause any conflicts with other mods as long as they're properly written. author: Syrchalis
prev: To duplicate the same item again, the item has to be first removed from the chest or the chest closed - this is to prevent items from infinitely duplicating themselves and causing lag or a crash[/*]
text: There is a very small amount of items that cannot be duplicated because they are created via local template. For example Firzu's Ring of Trading. This affects only 3-4 items. The mod overwrites some templates to make roughly half of these items able to be duplicated. Some legendaries will have a different name when duplicated, e.g. The Blood Of Lathander and Bloodthirst - while this is fixable I left it in as an easter egg.
next: https://i.imgur.com/bhEJPtf.png Weightless Effect Every item created in the ephemeral chest has a condition named "Weightless" which does exactly what you think. author: SilverCrossfire
heading: Important Compatibility Notice
prev: To allow Preserved Land to function without Concentration while still keeping its duration synced with the move spell, I had to rework the underlying mechanics. The solution uses a summoning‑stacking system, specifically the same stacking logic used by the US Intellect Devourer spell.
text: The only limitation is that the caster of Preserved Land cannot cast US at the same time. Casting one will automatically despawn the other, since both rely on the same stacking slot. This limitation should not affect other party members from casting US, and it won’t harm your save. It's simply a matter of one spell replacing the other when cast by the same character.
next: At the moment, summoning stacking is the only reliable method I’ve found to achieve the intended behavior, and US seemed like the least disruptive spell to borrow from due to how rarely it’s likely used, not part of a progression, and its stacking system appears isolated to that spell alone.

text: Why do I want this mod? author: OdeToAKite
heading: Known Bugs
prev: Due to how I implemented Imbue Emotion Longing, it has resulted in all zone shapes having a surface tooltip and Blast having a AOE radius . These mean nothing without Emotion Longing active.
text: If you respec, Shape will contain 2 copies of Blast at level 1. I believe this is a bug in the engine as in the back-end, that I can check, it only shows 1 copy. This will fix itself on gaining a new shape. Unbelievably I am the one at fault. This strange behaviour is what happens when you add the same container spell twice when they both have only one contained spell. - Fixed
next: I have a list of weird one off bugs I was never able to replicate, so I'd appreciate if people let me know if anything strange happens and how/when.
